note: LEADS.md Part P lead L3, STRATA_ATTN_WMMA_ROWS=2|4|8 (qsa_decode_attn_wmma.cu decode_attn_wmma_rows_kernel; CODED, HIP gfx1100 compile-checked, parity harness hip_decode_attn_wmma_parity extended, NOT RUN on a GPU): up to R query rows of one qsa_decode_attn_batch call per block, bit-identical per row to the one-row WMMA kernel (STRATA_ATTN_WMMA=1: neutral end to end at 36K T-019 / T-032, token forcing PASS T-300); the staged V rows and scales are shared across the rows when their selections are identical for the chunk. This is NOT hipfire's shared-K-scan verify kernel (their rows share a dense KV; ours select their own top-k cells, so K stays per row): the expected gain is the launch count and the V staging of a 3-9 row window, and it can lose (fewer blocks per launch; the int8 rows kernel spills 49 VGPRs against 0 for the one-row kernel). Judge the rows arms against `wmma`, not against `base`: wmma against base is the already measured switch, and a rows arm that does not beat `wmma` is dead whatever it does against `base`. The lever ran if the engine log has 'STRATA_ATTN_WMMA_ROWS='. The text of every wmma arm must equal `wmma`'s (bit-identical kernels); wmma against base may differ (FP32-level, not bitwise). First on the box: the parity harness `hip_decode_attn_wmma_parity` must print no 'NOT bit-identical'. Screen (--tier screen), then confirm with --block 3 --warmup 1 --outlier robust --reclaim-max 3 --reps 5. Lossy because of wmma itself: the token-forcing gate is spec 193.
